name: The St. Regis Florence
positioning: Historic palazzo hotel by Brunelleschi on the banks of the Arno, on Piazza Ognissanti in Florence
best_for: Travelers who want Renaissance history and art in a riverside palazzo
Suite guests who want St. Regis Butler Service

facts.text: The hotel stands on the banks of the Arno River, with views across to the Ponte Vecchio and the hills of Tuscany.
The hotel is on Piazza Ognissanti, a stone's throw from a Botticelli fresco.
The hotel is moments from Via de' Tornabuoni and its luxury boutiques.
The hotel is less than a 15-minute walk from the Duomo.
The building was originally home to the noble Giuntini family.
When the former palace became a hotel, it was first named the Grand Hotel Royal de la Paix.
Queen Victoria stayed at the hotel.
All suites have hand-carved gold leaf plaques and come in one of three color palettes: Medici, Florentine and Renaissance.
The Royal Suite draws inspiration from the Court of the Medici.
Bathrooms are finished in Carrara marble.
St. Regis Butler Service is available in all suites.
The hotel's signature cocktail, the Bloody Brunello, includes grappa made from the grapes used for Brunello di Montalcino.

highlights.text: The palace was designed by Filippo Brunelleschi around 1400.
The Sala delle Feste is a French-style ballroom inspired by the White Room in the nearby Pitti Palace.
The Art Deco-style Winter Garden was realized around 1922.
Cafe Ginori offers an afternoon tea curated by a tea sommelier, with Ginori porcelain.
The hotel offers a bespoke walking tour of Florence's fresco sites with an expert art-historian guide.

considerations.text: The spa is small, with a small hammam and a few spa suites.
Because it is a historic building, room accessibility is limited and varies by room category.
Kettles, coffee makers and irons are not permitted in rooms under historic-palace safety rules.
